label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: almost all of the team's rules were written by one member, in about a quarter of an hour
findings.why: The narrator reports with no I and no hindsight, so a busy reader gets a record line rather than the editor telling them what he now thinks of it.

findings.quote: A clock: each member wakes at its own minute. A hold anyone can pull.
findings.why: The practical pattern I would copy is delivered as a one-line aside; I would want it spelled out once in plain words (what the clock and the hold are) before the figure.

findings.quote: Nothing ran on the clock until there was a way to stop it.
findings.why: A strong line, but it sits in a run of short flat sentences with line 12 and the quoted Conductor lines, so the chapter's best takeaway reads as one beat among many.

findings.quote: None of the three had run. I pasted a short prompt into each member's own session, and each made its own.
findings.why: Short sentences stack here and the 'short prompt' is never shown, so I cannot copy what he pasted.

findings.quote: I made their tasks for them. That was a reach too far.
findings.why: The Conductor's line retells the correction the narrator just told in line 33 and again summarises in line 37, so it is said three times.

findings.quote: The check said no. It was right. The lines went in, and it said yes.
findings.why: Dev's line repeats the narrator's line 47 almost beat for beat, and 'the check' and 'the banner rule' are not explained to someone who has not read earlier chapters.

findings.quote: It is worth writing before the first scheduled run, not after.
findings.why: Reads as an instruction from above rather than from the editor's own experience; 'Something to try' is the one takeaway I wanted and it is only two sentences, with no first step I could do tomorrow.

findings.quote: Three decisions, close together, and the historian's record of the hour agrees.
findings.why: Announces three decisions, then the next three paragraphs list them again, and the Figure line 32 draws them a third time.

findings.quote: Here is the thing I most want you to take from the afternoon.
findings.why: Tells the reader what to take away; the following lines 100 to 103 are good and need no signpost.

findings.quote: That is the factory's economics in one afternoon.
findings.why: A 'That is the point' style opener after three short sentences, and the story is about reuse of the editor's own earlier sites, which my team cannot copy unless I have earlier sites; no takeaway for me except in the closing card.

findings.quote: the slide, its source commit and its data, copied unchanged and pinned to where they came from
findings.why: 'Pinned', 'source commit' and 'the player' are used before anything explains them, and I read this on a phone between meetings.

findings.quote: The player was not new; chapter 12 has where it came from.
findings.why: Points away to another chapter for the port, while the rest of the paragraph retells the studio and motion cards from earlier in this same chapter.

findings.quote: Same clock. Same hold. More hands on it.
findings.why: Three clipped fragments in a stage-direction voice; a good slogan but it opens the very section that needs plain explanation.

findings.quote: the owner of the brief, and one named person when the owner is away.
findings.why: My deal-breaker is a method that needs one central person: one brief owner who writes it and alone may lift the hold reads as exactly that, and the chapter does not say how a team of peers would avoid it.

findings.quote: came from the evening this book's team lost to the usage limit
findings.why: A paragraph of four 'came from' links to events I have not read, so I cannot check any of them; the lesson for my team is buried in references.

what_holds: 05-hour-two-the-rules-written.md: the hold existing before the first scheduled session is a clear, copyable pattern, and the correction of the conductor's own reach is honest and concrete.
14-port-not-rebuild.md: 'pull again before every push' as the price of longer sessions is a real, usable lesson about overlapping agents.

22-the-third-planned.md: brief, board and hold as the three shared things, with a stated wake-at-own-minute rule, is the nearest thing to a pattern my team could adopt tomorrow, and being labelled as a plan is honest.
notes: Answers to the persona questions: I get the factory (members, a clock, a hold anyone can pull) from 05, but who is in it and how it stops is spread across chapters. I would start with the hold and the pull-first rule. My team would need a worked example of the brief, the board and the hold as actual files, and a version without a single brief owner. Cast cards and clock lines are fine on a phone but long run-on record material is not visible, which is correct.
